To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the retinoids retinoic acid and retinal stimulate the proton transport of the uncoupling protein 1 (UCP) and that this stimulation is more potent than that exerted by fatty acids.
retinoids are powerful activators of the uncoupling protein UCP1 and that UCP1, UCP2 and possibly also UCP3 are all regulated by retinoid signalling.
retinoids are potent activators of proton transport by Ucp1 and Ucp2, and that Ucp2, like Ucp1, is a retinoid‐regulated mitochondrial uncoupling protein.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the regulation of UCP1 and the newly discovered UCP2 and their role in thermogenesis and energy expenditure.
the identification of regulators of the UCPs and with the understanding of the molecular basis of their action.
the regulation of proton transport by the three UCPs.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the UCP1 and 2 are activated by retinoic acid.
retinoids are the only known activators of UCP1 and that they are also the most potent activators.
UCP1 is a target of retinoids and that UCP2 is a retinoid‐sensitive protein.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the UCPs are regulated by a wide spectrum of compounds, and that the retinoids, in addition to being regulators of gene transcription, also act at the post‐transcriptional level.
retinoids regulate the proton transport by UCDs and that this regulation is mediated by the UCPs themselves.
retinoids regulate the uncoupling of oxidative phosphorylation through the UCPs.
The main takeaway from our work is that
UCP2 and the recently cloned UCP3 may be regulated by retinoic acid in a manner similar to that of UCP1.
UCP2 is a retinoid‐regulated proton transporter.
retinoids are potent regulators of UCP1 and of UCP2 and that they may play an important role in the regulation of energy expenditure.
